pnl_definition: Net trading revenue, firm-wide: trading gains net of direct trading costs (exchange, clearing, brokerage, financing), before compensation and other opex, by calendar year, in USD millions. Covers the Jump Trading group under Jump Financial, LLC, including Jump Crypto crypto market-making. Excludes Jump Capital (VC), venture or token-deal gains (e.g. the alleged Terra/LUNA profit) and regulatory settlements. Jump has never disclosed this figure, so every value here is an estimate.
headcount_definition: Total employees worldwide across all Jump Trading group offices (13 offices, 8 countries), as an approximate annual average. It is derived from the US 401(k) active participants of the US employer, Jump Operations LLC, at year-end, plus the UK subsidiary's filed average headcount, plus an assumed 15-30% for rest-of-world offices (Singapore, Hong Kong, Shanghai, Sydney, India, Amsterdam), which have no free filings. 2026 is the estimated average for Jan-Sep.
fx_note: All values are in USD. The UK subsidiary reports in USD (amounts in the evidence are USD or USD thousands, converted to USD millions here). The India figure (INR crore) is cited only for context and is not converted into any row.
methodology: Jump publishes no firm-wide revenue, and neither research lens found any press, filing or rating-agency figure for any year 2015-2026, so every PnL value is an estimate with wide bars. Each mid blends three approaches. (1) Headcount x peer median net trading revenue per head, from this project's IMC, Optiver and Virtu files, scaled by a Jump premium of about 1.2-1.5x. (2) A comp-ratio cross-check: global heads x UK staff cost per head (Companies House; about 0.9x for a cheaper global mix) divided by an assumed comp ratio of 30-60%, higher in weak years. (3) The independent year-by-year judgements of the press and primary lenses. Market regime sets the shape (lean 2016, 2017 and 2019; boom 2020-21; the 2022 crypto collapse; record volumes 2024-26), and the UK comp-per-head index sets the timing of Jump's own bonus cycle. Headcount is derived from primary US 401(k) and UK filings plus an assumed rest-of-world uplift.

entities.name: Jump Trading (firm-wide)
entities.description: The Jump Trading group under its ultimate parent Jump Financial, LLC. It includes Jump Trading LLC (US broker-dealer), Jump Operations LLC (US employer), Jump Trading International Ltd (UK service company), Jump Trading Europe B.V., the Asia-Pacific and India entities, and Jump Crypto (incl. Tai Mo Shan Ltd). It excludes Jump Capital (VC).

rows.notes: PnL: there is no firm-wide figure. Estimate: about 620 heads x peer median of about $1.25M per head (IMC 1.25, Optiver 1.13; Virtu's 3.4 is excluded as a pre-KCG outlier) x a Jump premium of about 1.5 gives about $1.15B. Both research lenses independently got $1.2-1.3B. Anchor: Bloomberg's 2010 US-entity operating revenue of $512M (net income $268M) from SEC filings. UK subsidiary net trading revenue of $159M (restated from $119M) is a Europe slice and is not added. Headcount: US 401(k) active participants 535 at year-end plus UK average 49, about 584, plus 15-30% for Singapore and other offices. Bloomberg's ~350 (early 2014, from a deleted website version) looks stale and widens the low tail.

PnL estimate. A lean-ish year for market makers (peer median about $1.15M per head). UK net trading revenue was flat at $158M. UK staff cost per head fell from about $1.4M to about $0.74M, but the UK mix changed (it was trader-heavy before), so this is not comparable. About 740 heads x about $1.0-1.5M per head gives a mid of $1.1B. The lenses got $1.0B (press) and $1.1B (primary). Headcount: US 578 at year-end plus UK 68 average, plus a rest-of-world uplift.

PnL estimate. A lean year: record-low volatility, peer per-head about $0.9M (IMC 0.90, Optiver 0.90). UK staff cost per head was about $0.56M, the trough of the series, which points to a small bonus pool. About 790 heads x about $1.1M gives $0.9B, matching both lenses. UK net trading revenue was $154M (Europe slice, not added). Headcount: US 565 plus UK 94 average, plus a rest-of-world uplift.

PnL estimate. A better year (the Feb 'Volmageddon' and the Q4 sell-off); peer median about $1.5M per head (IMC 1.34, Optiver 1.48, Virtu 1.91). UK net trading revenue rose 35% to $207M, the last full year the UK entity traded its own book. UK staff cost per head was about $0.62M. Mid $1.25B, against $1.1-1.2B from the lenses and about $1.8B from a pure peer-scaling approach. Headcount: US 535 plus UK 114 average, plus a rest-of-world uplift.

PnL estimate. A lean year; peer per-head about $0.9M (IMC 0.84, Virtu 0.92). From mid-2019 the UK entity became a cost-plus service company and EU trading moved to Jump Trading Europe B.V. (NL), so UK revenue of $159M is no longer trading revenue. UK staff cost per head was about $0.66M. Comp-ratio cross-check: about 840 heads x about $0.6M at 40-50% gives $1.0-1.25B. Mid $1.05B; the lenses got $1.0-1.2B. Headcount: US 588 plus UK 138 average, plus a rest-of-world uplift.

PnL estimate. A boom year (COVID volatility); peer per-head about $2.3M (IMC 2.24, Optiver 3.03, Virtu 2.28). UK staff cost per head rose about 75% to about $1.15M, consistent with a large bonus pool. Comp-ratio cross-check: about 920 heads x about $1.0M at 30-40% gives $2.4-3.2B. Pure peer scaling gives about $3.1B. Mid $2.75B; the lenses got $2.5-2.7B. UK revenue of $331M is transfer-pricing income and is excluded. Headcount: US 637 plus UK 154 average, plus a rest-of-world uplift.

PnL estimate. A boom year that includes crypto: Jump Crypto was active in crypto market-making and DeFi. Peer per-head about $2.0M. UK staff cost per head was about $1.20M, a series high until 2025 (directors' pay about $33.5M). Comp-ratio cross-check: about 1,090 x about $1.1M at 30-40% gives $2.9-3.9B. Mid $3.3B. It EXCLUDES the alleged ~$1.0-1.28B Terra/LUNA token gain (SEC complaint allegation; WSJ says about $1B). That gain spans 2021-22, only $73.45M was SEC-adjudicated, and it is a token-deal gain rather than trading revenue; the high bound leaves room for part of it. PrivCo ($120M revenue) and the insights4vc profit guess ($500M-1B) are rejected. Headcount: US 797 plus UK 183 average, plus a rest-of-world uplift.

PnL estimate. Crypto collapse and the Terra unwind: Wormhole bridge replenishment of about $320M (Feb) and FTX exposure of about $300M (Nov) weighed on Jump Crypto. Traditional market-making was solid (volatile markets; peer per-head about $1.5M, Optiver about $2.0M). In Mar 2022 Moody's cited a 'strong profitable track record' as Jump Financial added a $200M term loan, about $500M in total, for trading capital. UK staff cost per head fell about 11% to about $1.07M. Mid $2.4B; the lenses got $2.0B (press) and $2.8B (primary). Headcount: US 995 plus UK 246 average, plus a rest-of-world uplift. The welfare-plan count of 1,575 is erratic and rejected.

PnL estimate. A lean year (low volatility); peer per-head about $1.24M (IMC 0.99, Optiver 1.54, Virtu 1.24). UK staff cost per head fell again, to about $0.95M. Comp-ratio cross-check: about 1,540 x about $0.86M at 45-60% gives $2.2-2.9B. Pure peer scaling gives about $2.7B. The lenses got $1.5B (press) and $2.5B (primary). Mid $2.1B. US broker-dealer member's equity was $235M (balance sheet only). Headcount: US 1,010 plus UK 275 average (281 at year-end), plus a rest-of-world uplift.

PnL estimate. Record market volumes, but Jump's own signals are mixed. UK staff cost per head fell to about $0.84M, the lowest since 2019, while peers' per-head rose (median about $1.65M). Jump Crypto was scaled back, and Tai Mo Shan paid a $123.1M SEC settlement (a cost, not revenue). S&P revised its outlook to stable (BB-). Comp-ratio cross-check: about 1,560 x about $0.76M at 40-55% gives $2.1-2.9B. Pure peer scaling gives about $3.6B. The lenses got $2.4-2.5B. Mid $2.6B. UK revenue of $386M is service income and is excluded. Headcount: US 1,006 plus UK 288 average, plus a rest-of-world uplift.

PnL estimate. A probable record year. UK staff costs rose about 71% to $410M (wages up 73% to $342M) with a 'higher year-end accrued bonus pool', and UK cost per head was about $1.29M, a series high. Peers: IMC $1.76M, Optiver $2.31M and Virtu $2.18M per head; HRT is about $11M per head (press lens), the upper benchmark. Jump Financial issued $750M of debt in Feb 2025. Comp-ratio cross-check: about 1,720 x about $1.16M at 35-45% gives $4.4-5.7B. Pure peer scaling gives about $5.6B. The lenses got $4.0B (press) and $5.0B (primary). Mid $4.6B. UK revenue of $527M is service income and is excluded. India revenue of about INR 1,000 cr (Tracxn, unverified) is a slice only. ZoomInfo's $952M is rejected. Headcount: US 1,125 plus UK 336 at year-end gives 1,461, so the firm was about 1,800 at year-end; the average is shown.

YTD 2026-01-01 to 2026-09-30, ESTIMATED. There is no 2026 PnL data of any kind. Estimate: about 0.75 x the FY2025 mid, i.e. 9 months at the 2025 run-rate in a continuing record-volume regime, giving about $3.4B with wide bars. This matches how peer 2026 YTD values were built (IMC and Optiver are run-rate estimates too). Headcount: the homepage says '2000+ employees' (fetched 2026-10-08; a marketing round number that may include interns or contractors). Built In says 1,488 and newsletters say about 1,500-1,600. The primary US+UK floor was already 1,461 at year-end 2025. The Jan-Sep 2026 average is estimated at about 1,900.

ytd_2026.description: ESTIMATED, NOT REPORTED. Jump publishes no results, and no 2026 PnL datapoint of any kind was found as of 2026-10-08. The YTD PnL is about 0.75 x the FY2025 mid ($4.6B), i.e. 9 months at the 2025 run-rate in a continuing record-volume regime: mid $3.4B, range $1.6-5.8B. Headcount (about 1,900, range 1,650-2,150) combines the year-end 2025 primary US+UK floor of 1,461, an uplift for rest-of-world offices, and the homepage claim of 2000+ employees (fetched 2026-10-08).

caveats: Every PnL value is an estimate: Jump has never published group revenue, and no top-tier press figure exists for 2015-2026. The last hard figures are for the US entity in 2008 and 2010 (Bloomberg, from SEC filings).

UK Companies House figures (revenue $352M 2023, $386M 2024, $527M 2025; headcount 275-336) cover the UK subsidiary only. From 2019 that revenue is cost-plus transfer-pricing income, so it is used here only as a comp-per-head index and is never added to group PnL.
US DOL 401(k) counts (about 1,010-1,125) are US-only active plan participants. They may lag new hires and exclude interns and contractors.
Terra/LUNA gains (alleged $1.28B, WSJ about $1B, SEC-adjudicated $73.45M) and the $123.1M Tai Mo Shan settlement are excluded from PnL. So are Jump Capital and venture/token gains.
